name: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory
reason: Abuse: assign Global Administrator (or any directory role) to any principal. Critical: direct tenant admin with no intermediate hop.

name: AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: grant any app role (including RoleManagement or Mail.Send) to any SP—including self. Critical: universal permission escalation.

name: Application.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: rotate credentials and redirect URIs on any app—become that app in the tenant. Critical: impersonation of arbitrary first- and third-party apps.

name: DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: create AllPrincipals or broad delegated grants for arbitrary scopes. Critical: tenant-wide consent equivalent without per-user phishing.

name: Domain.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: alter or add domains in the tenant. Critical: tenant takeover risk.

name: Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess
reason: Abuse: add exclusions, weaken MFA, or block admins from signing in. Critical: defeats tenant-wide access controls.

name: PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureAD
reason: Abuse: approve or materialize privileged role assignments via PIM. Critical: GA-equivalent without standing assignment.

name: DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: grant Intune admin roles or widen scope tags to own account. High: full device-estate control short of Entra GA.

name: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.CloudPC
reason: Abuse: own Cloud PC RBAC—compromise Windows 365 admin plane. High: major segment, not entire Entra directory.

name: DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: same Intune RBAC writes but only in user-delegated context. Low: requires already-privileged sign-in; AllPrincipals here is a weak signal.

name: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.CloudPC
reason: Abuse: Cloud PC RBAC changes as the signed-in user. Low: bounded by users existing Cloud PC admin rights; rare as org-wide grant.

name: Directory.AccessAsUser.All
reason: Abuse: act on the directory with the full rights of the signed-in user. Only abusable when that identity holds an admin role (e.g. Global Administrator): delegated access never exceeds the user's own rights. High: with an admin signing in, the app holds that admin's full directory power.

name: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory
reason: Abuse: assign directory roles, including Global Administrator, as the signed-in user. Only abusable when that identity holds Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator. High: one admin sign-in to the app is enough to escalate.

name: Application.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: add credentials to apps and service principals as the signed-in user. Only tenant-wide when that identity holds an admin role (e.g. Application Administrator); otherwise limited to apps the user owns. High: with an admin signing in, any app can be impersonated.

name: AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: grant app roles (such as RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory) to any service principal as the signed-in user. Only abusable when that identity holds an admin role that can grant consent (e.g. Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator). High: one admin sign-in turns it into permanent app-only escalation.

name: Mail.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: read, change, and delete mail as the signed-in user—consent-phishing staple for inbox rules, evidence removal, and exfil. No admin role needed; limited to mailboxes the user can already open, and an Exchange admin role does not widen it. Medium: per-user blast radius.

name: Mail.Send
reason: Abuse: send mail as the signed-in user for internal phishing and BEC. No admin role needed; limited to the user's own mailbox and mailboxes they have Send As on. Medium: per-user blast radius.

name: Files.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: read, overwrite, or encrypt every file the signed-in user can reach—OneDrive plus shared SharePoint content. No admin role needed; limited to the user's own access. Medium: per-user blast radius, but shared sites widen it.

name: EWS.AccessAsUser.All
reason: Abuse: full EWS access to the signed-in user's mailbox—read, send, rules, and delegates. No admin role needed; limited to mailboxes the user can already open. Medium: per-user blast radius.

name: Directory.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: create users, reset attributes, manipulate groups—often chains to GA via role-assignable groups or owned objects. High: below direct RoleManagement but still org-wide write.

name: PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup
reason: Abuse: make identities eligible for privileged groups—path to Azure RBAC or app access via group. High: not directory-role assignment but strong pivot.

name: GroupMember.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: add self or ally to any group—dangerous only if exploitable privileged groups exist. Low: permission is extremely common; signal is hygiene, not inherent tier-0.

name: UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: strip or add MFA methods for any user—silent takeover of chosen accounts. High: targeted, not tenant-wide admin, but no user cooperation needed.

name: Mail.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: read, delete, or alter all mail in every mailbox—evidence destruction and mass exfil. High: no send-as-anyone (see Mail.Send) but write scope across all mailboxes.

name: Mail.Send
reason: Abuse: send as any mailbox with tenant mail trust. Critical: BEC and phishing at arbitrary scale without compromised user passwords.

name: Contacts.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: create or overwrite contacts in every mailbox—spoof display names, phone numbers, and SMTP addresses so users trust forged senders or call attacker numbers. High: social engineering without Mail.Send.

name: Mail.Read
reason: Abuse: copy all mail app-only—total confidentiality breach. Low: identical technical blast radius as many backup/DLP products; alert alone is low-fidelity without app reputation.

name: User.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: password reset and profile takeover for any user. Medium: catastrophic if abused but routinely required by IDM/provisioning; narrower than directory-role grant.

name: Directory.Read.All
reason: Abuse: full tenant enumeration for targeting. Low: read-only; nearly every SaaS integration requests it—weak discriminator for malicious apps.

name: eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: alter holds, cases, review sets—spoliation and access to highest-sensitivity legal data. Critical: write on legal pipeline plus massive content exposure.

name: eDiscovery.Read.All
reason: Abuse: read investigation and hold-adjacent content—sensitive exfil. Medium: no hold tampering; fewer vendors than Mail.Read but still specialized category.

name: Chat.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: read or modify all Teams 1:1/group chats app-only. Medium: broad collaboration compromise; Microsoft may gate some APIs—below mail/send for typical abuse economics.

name: Chat.Read.All
reason: Abuse: exfiltrate all private and group Teams chats. Medium: read-only; retention and compliance vendors legitimately drive volume.

name: ChannelMessage.Read.All
reason: Abuse: read every Teams channel message—org-wide comms and IP exfil. Medium: supervision/archiving vendors; no write path.

name: CallRecords.Read.All
reason: Abuse: map who called whom and when—metadata surveillance. Low: no content; CDR and contact-center integrations normalize this permission.

name: AuditLog.Read.All
reason: Abuse: learn defender actions and admin activity to evade detection. Low: SIEM exports need it; read-only and ubiquitous on security tooling.

name: ThreatHunting.Read.All
reason: Abuse: run KQL across M365 Defender corpus—mailbox, device, and identity telemetry harvest. Medium: exceeds most integrations; MDR/MSSP-typical, not commodity SaaS.

name: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All
reason: Abuse: remote wipe, PIN reset, or lockout on all Intune devices—business continuity destruction. Critical: device fleet availability, not just data theft.

name: DeviceManagementServiceConfig.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: enroll attacker hardware (e.g. Autopilot import), change enrollment boundaries. Medium: serious device-trust impact but standard for UEM onboarding products.

name: Files.Read.All
reason: Abuse: read every file in SharePoint and OneDrive. Low: same capability as many backup and search products—low signal without vendor context.

name: Files.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: delete or encrypt all tenant documents—ransomware analogue. Critical: tenant-wide file integrity and availability.

name: Sites.FullControl.All
reason: Abuse: script, admin, and content control on every site—superset of file R/W. Critical: SharePoint tenant compromise.

name: Sites.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: read/write all list items and documents without full site-admin shell. High: mass exfil and tamper; one step below FullControl for some attack paths.

name: Sites.Manage.All
reason: Abuse: destroy or recreate lists/libraries tenant-wide—availability and structure sabotage. High: often paired with data attacks.

name: SharePointTenantSettings.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: loosen sharing, guest, or OneDrive policies—opens data exfil channels. High: policy-layer, not direct file read.

name: TermStore.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: corrupt managed metadata—breaks classification, search, and retention semantics. High: integrity across content estate.

name: Sites.Read.All
reason: Abuse: read all site and list content—document exfil via Graph sites API. Low: overlaps Files.Read.All use cases; noisy for alerting.

name: Sites.FullControl.All
reason: Abuse: native SPO/REST full control on all site collections—same impact as Graph Sites.FullControl on SP resource. Critical.

name: Sites.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: app-only R/W all sites via SharePoint API—parallel to Graph Sites.ReadWrite. High.

name: Sites.Manage.All
reason: Abuse: structural destruction across all sites via SPO resource. High.

name: TermStore.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: tenant term store rewrite via SPO resource—metadata integrity. High.

name: SharePointTenantSettings.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: loosen sharing, guest, or OneDrive policies via the SPO resource—opens data exfil channels. High: same as the Graph version.

name: Sites.Read.All
reason: Abuse: read all site and list content via the SPO REST API. Low: same as the Graph version; noisy for alerting.

name: Organization.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: change tenant branding, partner relationships, and org metadata—phishing lures and trust abuse. High: not direct GA but broad org-level write.

name: Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration
reason: Abuse: alter token lifetime, claims mapping, HRD, and issuance policies—authentication and token-trust manipulation. High: tier-0-adjacent; cited in consent and federation abuse research.

name: Policy.ReadWrite.CrossTenantAccess
reason: Abuse: change cross-tenant access defaults—expand guest/B2B trust surface. High: lateral movement into partner tenants or inbound abuse.

name: User.Invite.All
reason: Abuse: invite arbitrary B2B guests—persistence and lateral access. Medium: powerful but common on collaboration portals; volume-based risk.

name: AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: redefine scoped admin boundaries and membership—segment RBAC takeover. High: fewer vendors than GroupMember; meaningful policy impact.

name: SecurityEvents.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: modify security events—evasion and blind defenders. High: integrity of SecOps pipeline.

name: SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: alter M365 Defender incidents—close or corrupt case workflow. High: SOC integrity.

name: SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: resolve or reclassify Defender alerts—hide active attacks from the SOC. High: integrity of SecOps triage.

name: IdentityRiskyUser.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: dismiss risky-user state—clears ID Protection signals for compromised accounts. High: direct impact on identity SOC.

name: DeviceManagementConfiguration.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: deploy malicious Intune compliance or configuration profiles to all scoped devices. High: device compromise at scale short of wipe.

name: DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: read or alter managed device inventory and properties. Medium: excludes wipe/passcode reset but broad device recon and tamper.

name: IdentityUserFlow.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: change B2C/CIAM user flows—authentication UX and logic tampering. High: where External ID flows are used.

name: OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: create or hijack meetings as the app—meeting phishing and join-link abuse. Medium: cited in OAuth/consent abuse alongside mail and calendar.

name: Calls.AccessMedia.All
reason: Abuse: access live call media streams app-only—wiretap-class eavesdropping. Critical: confidentiality of voice/video.

name: CustomSecAttributeAssignment.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: rewrite security attribute assignments—ABAC and access-control decisions based on attributes can be subverted. High: niche but high impact where CSAs gate access.

name: RoleAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.Directory
reason: Abuse: create an active PIM assignment of Global Administrator for a controlled account. Critical: direct tenant admin via the PIM API.

name: RoleEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.Directory
reason: Abuse: make a controlled account eligible for Global Administrator, then activate it. Critical: one activation away from tenant admin.

name: RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.Directory
reason: Abuse: strip MFA, approval, and justification requirements from Entra role activation. High: removes PIM guardrails that block other escalation paths.

name: PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup
reason: Abuse: add a controlled account as owner or member of a role-assignable group that holds Global Administrator. Critical: direct tenant admin via PIM for Groups.

name: PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup
reason: Abuse: create active PIM for Groups assignments to role-assignable groups holding privileged roles. Critical: same path as PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup.

name: RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup
reason: Abuse: remove MFA and approval requirements from PIM for Groups activation. High: removes guardrails on privileged group membership.

name: PrivilegedAccess.ReadWrite.AzureResources
reason: Abuse: legacy PIM API for Azure resource role assignments. Low: retired API not known to work app-only; flag as hygiene.

name: Policy.ReadWrite.PermissionGrant
reason: Abuse: create a permission grant policy that lets the app obtain RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory. Critical: self-escalation to tenant admin.

name: Application.ReadUpdate.All
reason: Abuse: add credentials to any existing app or service principal and act as it. Critical: same impersonation path as Application.ReadWrite.All.

name: Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy
reason: Abuse: add credentials to apps this app owns and inherit their permissions. High: limited to owned apps, but a privileged owned app is a full escalation.

name: DelegatedAdminRelationship.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: in a partner tenant, add a controlled account to groups mapped in GDAP relationships and assume their roles in customer tenants. Critical: Global Administrator across customer tenants.

name: EntitlementManagement.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: remove approval from an access package that grants a privileged role, then request it with a controlled account. High: escalation via Identity Governance.

name: Group.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: change owners and members of any non-role-assignable group, including groups granting Azure RBAC or app access. Medium: very common on collaboration tools; real risk depends on what groups grant.

name: Group-OnPremisesSyncBehavior.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: flip a group between cloud-managed and synced to move control between Entra and on-premises AD. Medium: needs on-premises admin access for the full path.

name: Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod
reason: Abuse: enable weak or attacker-friendly methods (TAP, SMS, QR) tenant-wide. High: enabler for account takeover via authentication method permissions.

name: UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: issue a Temporary Access Pass for any user and sign in as them. High: silent targeted takeover, same as UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All.

name: UserAuthMethod-Phone.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: set an attacker phone number on any user and sign in with SMS one-time codes. High: targeted takeover where SMS sign-in is allowed.

name: UserAuthMethod-HardwareOATH.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: register an attacker-held OATH token on any user and pass MFA as them. High: targeted takeover where hardware OATH is enabled.

name: UserAuthMethod-QR.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: generate a QR code and PIN for any user and sign in as them. High: targeted takeover where QR code sign-in is enabled.

name: User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: reset the password of users the app can manage. High: purpose-built for password resets, so a grant is a stronger signal than User.ReadWrite.All.

name: User.EnableDisableAccount.All
reason: Abuse: disable every account, including break-glass, and hold the tenant to ransom. High: tenant-wide availability impact comparable to Global Administrator.

name: User.DeleteRestore.All
reason: Abuse: delete every account, including break-glass, and hold the tenant to ransom. High: tenant-wide availability impact comparable to Global Administrator.

name: SecurityIdentitiesActions.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: disable accounts or mark every user compromised through Defender for Identity actions. High: tenant-wide availability impact.

name: SignInIdentifier.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: change a controlled account's UPN to fall into a dynamic group with privileged access. Medium: depends on dynamic group rules in the tenant.

name: DeviceManagementScripts.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: deploy PowerShell or shell scripts that run as SYSTEM on managed devices, including admin workstations. High: code execution across the device fleet.

name: Synchronization.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: reconfigure provisioning and cloud sync jobs and their attribute mappings. Medium: abuse paths are not well researched, but the scope reaches identity sync.

name: Calendars.ReadWrite.All
reason: Abuse: read/write every mailbox calendar on EXO resource—meeting intel, invite injection, availability exfil. High: OAuth abuse surface per Microsoft/defender guidance.

name: MailboxSettings.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: alter forwarding, OOF, locale, and mailbox settings tenant-wide—persistence and mail redirection without Mail.Send. Medium: common on EXO tooling.

name: Exchange.ManageAsApp
reason: Abuse: full Exchange org administration as app—mail flow, RBAC, mailboxes, transport. Critical: mail-plane tier-0; no Graph equivalent granularity.

name: Exchange.ManageAsAppV2
reason: Abuse: preview name of Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp—grant folder permissions (Inbox, Calendar) and Send on behalf on any mailbox the app's Exchange role covers. High: persistent mailbox access and BEC that survives app removal; needs an Exchange RBAC role.

name: Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp
reason: Abuse: Exchange Admin API as app—grant folder permissions (Inbox, Calendar) and Send on behalf on any mailbox the app's Exchange role covers. Critical: persistent mailbox access and BEC that survives app removal; needs an Exchange RBAC role. The rating is partly forward-looking: Microsoft is expanding this API to replace EWS, so new endpoints are expected to land under this same permission without a new consent.

name: Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage
reason: Abuse: consented app adds attacker access to the user's folders or Send on behalf list via the Exchange Admin API. Medium: user-consentable, and the delegation persists after the grant is revoked.

name: Exchange.ManageV2
reason: Abuse: preview name of Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage—consented app adds attacker access to the user's folders or Send on behalf list. Medium: user-consentable, and the delegation persists after the grant is revoked.

name: Exchange.Manage
reason: Abuse: run Exchange Online PowerShell cmdlets as the signed-in user—transport rules, forwarding, mailbox permissions. Only abusable when that identity holds an Exchange admin role; cmdlets are limited to the user's own Exchange RBAC. High: with an Exchange admin signing in, the app holds the whole mail plane.

name: EWS.AccessAsUser.All
reason: Abuse: full EWS access to the signed-in user's mailbox via the Exchange Online resource. No admin role needed; limited to mailboxes the user can already open. Medium: same as the Graph version.

name: Mail.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: read, change, and delete mail as the signed-in user via the Exchange Online resource. No admin role needed; limited to mailboxes the user can already open. Medium: same as the Graph version.

name: Mail.Send
reason: Abuse: send mail as the signed-in user via the Exchange Online resource. No admin role needed; limited to the user's own mailbox and mailboxes they have Send As on. Medium: same as the Graph version.

name: full_access_as_app
reason: Abuse: EWS full access to every mailbox—read, change, delete, and send as any user. Critical: the app-only mailbox takeover used in high-profile intrusions.

name: Mail.Send
reason: Abuse: send as any mailbox through the Exchange Online resource. Critical: same BEC impact as Graph Mail.Send.

name: Mail.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: read, change, or delete mail in every mailbox through the Exchange Online resource. High: same as Graph Mail.ReadWrite.

name: Mail.Read
reason: Abuse: read all mail through the Exchange Online resource. Low: same as Graph Mail.Read; common on backup and archiving products.

name: Contacts.ReadWrite
reason: Abuse: forge contacts in every mailbox through the Exchange Online resource. High: same social-engineering impact as Graph Contacts.ReadWrite.

name: SMTP.SendAsApp
reason: Abuse: send mail over SMTP AUTH as mailboxes the app was granted. Medium: needs per-mailbox Exchange permissions for the service principal.

name: IMAP.AccessAsApp
reason: Abuse: read and change mail over IMAP in mailboxes the app was granted. Medium: needs per-mailbox Exchange permissions for the service principal.

name: POP.AccessAsApp
reason: Abuse: download mail over POP from mailboxes the app was granted. Medium: needs per-mailbox Exchange permissions for the service principal.

name: Global Administrator
reason: Abuse: everything in Entra ID and every Microsoft 365 service, including elevating to all Azure subscriptions. Critical: an app holding it is a standing tenant admin with no user, MFA or PIM in the way.

name: Privileged Role Administrator
reason: Abuse: assign any directory role, including Global Administrator, and grant consent for any permission to any app. Critical: one step from tenant admin.

name: Privileged Authentication Administrator
reason: Abuse: reset the password and authentication methods of any user, Global Administrators included, then sign in as them. Critical: takeover of any account.

name: Partner Tier2 Support
reason: Abuse: reset passwords of any user including Global Administrators, manage domains and role assignments. Critical: deprecated role that should not be assigned to anything.

name: Customer Delegated Admin Relationship Administrator
reason: Abuse: accept a GDAP relationship from any partner, giving that partner's staff admin roles in this tenant. Critical: hands tenant administration to an outside organisation.

name: Application Administrator
reason: Abuse: add credentials to any app or service principal and act as it, and consent to delegated permissions for everyone. Critical: adding a secret to any app that holds RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All turns this into Global Administrator; no app needs it to do its own job.

name: Cloud Application Administrator
reason: Abuse: add credentials to any app or service principal and act as it, and consent to delegated permissions for everyone. Critical: adding a secret to any app that holds RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All turns this into Global Administrator; no app needs it to do its own job.

name: Hybrid Identity Administrator
reason: Abuse: change domain federation and sync settings so a token signer the attacker controls is trusted for any user. Critical: a federation backdoor signs in as anyone.

name: Domain Name Administrator
reason: Abuse: add domains and configure federation on them, then sign in as any user of a federated domain. Critical: a federation backdoor.

name: External Identity Provider Administrator
reason: Abuse: configure identity providers and domain federation that the tenant trusts for sign-in. Critical: can introduce a trusted sign-in source the attacker controls.

name: Security Administrator
reason: Abuse: change Conditional Access, ID Protection, Defender and domain federation settings. Critical: can switch off the controls that protect every sign-in.

name: Conditional Access Administrator
reason: Abuse: disable or exclude accounts from every Conditional Access policy. Critical: removes MFA and device requirements tenant-wide.

name: Exchange Administrator
reason: Abuse: grant itself access to any mailbox, add forwarding and transport rules, export mail. Critical: all mail in the tenant.

name: SharePoint Administrator
reason: Abuse: make itself admin of any site or OneDrive and read or share every file. Critical: all files in the tenant.

name: Intune Administrator
reason: Abuse: push scripts and apps to every managed device and read BitLocker keys and local admin passwords. Critical: code execution on all managed devices.

name: Authentication Policy Administrator
reason: Abuse: weaken the authentication methods policy and tenant-wide MFA settings. High: lowers the bar for every sign-in.

name: Authentication Extensibility Administrator
reason: Abuse: create custom authentication extensions that call out to an attacker endpoint during sign-in and token issuance. High: can alter tokens for apps that use them.

name: User Administrator
reason: Abuse: reset passwords of users and limited admins, create, delete and disable users, and manage group membership. High: account takeover of most users, including app owners.

name: Authentication Administrator
reason: Abuse: reset passwords and authentication methods of non-admins, then sign in as them. High: account takeover of most users, including app owners.

name: Helpdesk Administrator
reason: Abuse: reset passwords of non-admins and read BitLocker keys. High: account takeover of most users.

name: Password Administrator
reason: Abuse: reset passwords of non-admins. High: account takeover of most users.

name: Entra SOC Identity Responder
reason: Abuse: reset passwords, revoke sessions and disable users. High: account takeover or lockout of users.

name: Partner Tier1 Support
reason: Abuse: reset non-admin passwords, add app credentials and manage users and groups. High: deprecated role that should not be assigned to anything.

name: Tenant Governance Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage cross-tenant access and, through the Tenant Governance app, service principals, consent grants and app role assignments. High: can grant access to tenant resources.

name: Directory Synchronization Accounts
reason: Abuse: write synced users, including their password hashes, so it can set the password of any synchronised account and sign in as it. High: takeover of every hybrid account; only Microsoft Entra Connect should hold it.

name: Directory Writers
reason: Abuse: create users, change group membership and create OAuth2 permission grants. High: intended for apps, but enough to grant itself or others more access.

name: Groups Administrator
reason: Abuse: change membership of any group that is not role-assignable, including groups that grant access to apps and data. High: access to whatever those groups unlock.

name: Identity Governance Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage access packages, group membership and app role assignments. High: can grant access to apps and groups.

name: Lifecycle Workflows Administrator
reason: Abuse: create workflows that run tasks against users, such as changing groups or disabling accounts. High: automated changes across many users.

name: Compliance Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage compliance features and all features in the Exchange admin center. High: broad reach into mail and data governance.

name: Exchange Recipient Administrator
reason: Abuse: change any recipient, including mailbox permissions and forwarding. High: can open up mailboxes.

name: Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator
reason: Abuse: restore and manage Microsoft 365 Backup for mail, SharePoint and OneDrive. High: can overwrite content or change what is protected.

name: Cloud Device Administrator
reason: Abuse: read BitLocker keys and local admin passwords, and disable or delete devices. High: unlocks devices and their local admin accounts.

name: Windows 365 Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage Cloud PCs and security groups. High: control of Cloud PCs and the groups that target them.

name: Teams Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage Teams, external access and all Microsoft 365 groups. High: can open Teams to outsiders and change group membership.

name: Power Platform Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage all Power Platform environments, flows and data loss prevention policies. High: access to business data and automations.

name: Fabric Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage all Fabric and Power BI workspaces. High: access to business reporting data.

name: AI Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage Copilot, agents, agent identities and admin consent request policies. High: controls what agents can do in the tenant.

name: Agent ID Administrator
reason: Abuse: manage agent identities, including their credentials and role assignments. High: can act as any agent identity.

name: Security Operator
reason: Abuse: reset passwords, disable users and manage Defender for Endpoint. High: can lock users out and act on devices.

name: Global Reader
reason: Abuse: read every setting in every Microsoft 365 admin center, and BitLocker keys. High: a full map of the tenant's defences for an attacker.

name: Security Reader
reason: Abuse: read security alerts, sign-in and audit logs, Conditional Access and BitLocker keys. Low suspicion: common for security tools. High: shows an attacker what is monitored.

name: Reports Reader
reason: Abuse: read sign-in logs, audit logs and usage reports. Low suspicion: common for reporting tools.

name: Directory Readers
reason: Abuse: read users, groups, apps and role memberships. Low suspicion: Microsoft recommends it for apps that need directory read access.

name: Billing Administrator
reason: Abuse: make purchases and manage subscriptions and payment details. Medium: financial and licensing changes.

name: License Administrator
reason: Abuse: remove licences from users, cutting off their mail and apps. Low suspicion: common for licensing tools.

name: B2C IEF Keyset Administrator
reason: Abuse: upload or replace the token signing and federation keys of the Identity Experience Framework. Critical: in a B2C tenant, forge tokens for any user.

name: B2C IEF Policy Administrator
reason: Abuse: rewrite custom sign-in policies to send credentials or claims to an attacker endpoint or skip MFA. High: controls how every B2C user signs in.

name: Application Developer
reason: Abuse: register new apps regardless of the 'Users can register applications' setting and hold their credentials as owner. High: builds in-tenant backdoor apps that wait for consent and look home-grown in consent prompts.

name: Entra Backup Administrator
reason: Abuse: restore directory objects and settings from an older snapshot, such as Conditional Access policies or app credentials from before a hardening change. High: silently rolls back security configuration.

name: Edge Administrator
reason: Abuse: force-install a browser extension on every managed Edge through the Edge management service. High: an extension reads every page, cookie and session token users have open.

name: Office Apps Administrator
reason: Abuse: push Cloud Policy settings to every Office install, such as enabling macros from the internet or trusted locations. High: opens the path for code execution on users' machines.

name: Global Secure Access Administrator
reason: Abuse: change traffic forwarding, web filtering and Private Access apps, publishing internal resources or disabling filtering. High: controls the network path to internal apps and the internet.

name: Cloud App Security Administrator
reason: Abuse: switch off Defender for Cloud Apps policies, session controls and alerts, and run governance actions that suspend users. High: blinds the detection that would spot data theft.

name: Azure Information Protection Administrator
reason: Abuse: change sensitivity labels and their protection settings so protected content is no longer encrypted or is shared with outsiders. High: removes the protection on labelled data.

name: Attribute Assignment Administrator
reason: Abuse: set custom security attributes on users and apps, which Conditional Access app filters and Azure ABAC conditions key on. High: can move an app out of a policy or into an access condition.

name: Attack Simulation Administrator
reason: Abuse: send simulated phishing with arbitrary links and payloads to every user, delivered past the mail filters. High: a trusted delivery path for real phishing.

name: Exchange Backup Administrator
reason: Abuse: restore any mailbox from Microsoft 365 Backup, including granular restores, and change backup policies. High: can overwrite mail or stop protecting it.

name: SharePoint Backup Administrator
reason: Abuse: restore any site or OneDrive from Microsoft 365 Backup and change backup policies. High: can overwrite files or stop protecting them.

name: Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator
